main_text.l: De excellentia & vi
amoris coniugalis videtur etiam illud dictū
Ecclef.36. Pulchritudo mulieris vultum ex-
hilarat, omnemque humanam iucunditatem
excellit. Si linguae eius inest comitas, leni-
tas & salubritas, maritus eius non est filijs ho-
minum comparandus. Item illud Dauidis,
2.Reg.1. Moeror est mihi propter te frater mi
Ionathan: gratisimus enim mihi fuisti: mi-
rabilis(id est, praestans & singularis) factus

Est autem, inquit Rabi Leui, mulieris amor
tam fortis, ut si maritus eam iam percusserit,
& illi maledixerit, non possit vel in modico

page.notes: The Greek passage is set in small italic type and is blurred; only fragments can be read with confidence. Words marked [?] are doubtful, and the longest stretch in the middle of the second Greek line is illegible. The Greek quotation is attributed to Hierocles, but its text was not copied from memory. The Latin is clear throughout. The last line ends with "nō" and the sentence continues on the next page. No catchword is printed.
